# Fractal Designs — Barnsley Fern

A Python program that renders a Barnsley fern using an iterated function system (IFS), plotted with NumPy and Matplotlib.

## Fractal Type(s) Implemented

**Barnsley fern** — generated by repeatedly applying one of four affine transformations (stem, small leaflets, left leaflet, right leaflet) to a point, each chosen at random according to a fixed probability:

| Transform | Purpose                        | Probability |
|-----------|---------------------------------|-------------|
| f1        | Stem                            | 1%          |
| f2        | Successively smaller leaflets   | 85%         |
| f3        | Largest left-hand leaflet       | 7%          |
| f4        | Largest right-hand leaflet      | 7%          |

Starting from the origin `(0, 0)`, each new point is generated by applying the chosen transform to the previous point. Over hundreds of thousands of iterations the accumulated points converge to the fern shape.

## Tools, Languages & Libraries

* Python 3.x
* `numpy` — random sampling and point generation
* `matplotlib` — rendering and image export

## Setup & Run

```
git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/Fractal-Designs.git
cd Fractal-Designs
pip install numpy matplotlib
python barnsley_fern.py
```

No other setup is needed. Running the script saves `barnsley_fern.png` in the working directory and displays the plot.

Adjust the number of points or the color in `plot_fern()`:

```
pts = barnsley_fern(n_points=1_000_000)
plot_fern(pts)
```
